title: WHY ARE PEOPLE QUICK TO ANSWER WITHOUT READING THE ARTICLE FIRST?
paragraphs: WHY ARE PEOPLE QUICK TO ANSWER WITHOUT READING THE ARTICLE FIRST?
The Three Seconds That Reveal the Human Heart
There is a strange moment that happens every day across the internet.
A biblical truth is carefully explained.
And before the reader could have possibly reached the second paragraph...
The question is no longer whether people read.
The question is why so many people seem determined to answer before they understand.
What does God think about it?
Because this is not merely a social media problem.
This is a human heart problem.
Scripture was already exposing this tendency.
The Bible knew we would do this.
God knew we would do this.
And He warned us about it.
The ancient Hebrew wisdom literature contains one of the most devastating observations ever written about human behavior.
"He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him."
The Hebrew text is remarkably direct.

"מֵשִׁיב דָּבָר בְּטֶרֶם יִשְׁמָע"
(Meshiv davar beterem yishma)
God says even that is already folly.
The Hebrew word translated as "folly" is אִוֶּלֶת (ivvelet).
It describes foolishness that comes from moral deficiency rather than intellectual deficiency.
The problem is not that people cannot understand.
The problem is that they often do not want to.
They want to respond more than they want to listen.
Because most people believe they are searching for truth.
Yet often they are searching for confirmation.
They are not reading to learn.
They are not listening to understand.
And somewhere in the process, truth becomes the casualty.
A husband stops listening halfway through his wife's sentence because he is already preparing his defense.
A wife hears only the first few words and immediately assumes she knows what comes next.
The tragedy is older than the internet.
It reaches all the way back to Eden.
When the serpent approached Eve, he did not begin by teaching.
He created a conclusion before understanding.
Replace careful hearing with emotional reaction.
Humanity has been struggling with that temptation ever since.
The Apostle James addressed the same issue centuries later.
Writing in Greek, he offered what may be one of the most urgently needed commands for modern culture.
"Let every person be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger."

ἔστω δὲ πᾶς ἄνθρωπος ταχὺς εἰς τὸ ἀκοῦσαι
(estō de pas anthrōpos tachys eis to akousai)
"Let every person be swift to hear."
Yet modern culture has reversed the entire sequence.
Today speed is often mistaken for intelligence.
The fastest response often gets the most visibility.
He measures what happens before the response.
The qualities that rarely go viral.
Many people answer before reading because reading requires surrender.
To truly read something means accepting the possibility that you may be wrong.
That possibility is threatening to human pride.
And every one of us carries both tendencies inside our hearts.
This is why Jesus consistently astonished people.
When others rushed to conclusions, He saw deeper.
When crowds condemned the woman caught in adultery, Jesus saw a soul.
When religious leaders dismissed tax collectors, Jesus saw future disciples.
When others saw fishermen, Jesus saw apostles.
When others saw failures, Jesus saw redemption.
Because heaven does not evaluate people at first glance.
And perhaps that is the hidden danger of answering before reading.
We begin treating people the way God never treated us.
Imagine if God interrupted your story after the first chapter.
Imagine if He stopped reading after your worst mistake.
Imagine if He judged your entire life based solely on your lowest moment.
None of us would survive such judgment.
Yet many people extend to others far less patience than God extended to them.
The Gospel itself is a testimony against premature conclusions.
Humanity looked at a crucified Christ and assumed defeat.
But they had reached a conclusion before the story was finished.
Three days later the empty tomb exposed how wrong they were.
The greatest victory in human history looked like failure to people who stopped reading too soon.
Some people have stopped reading God's work in their own lives too early.
And perhaps someone reading this right now has been tempted to quit because the story feels unfinished.
Do not judge your life by a page God has not finished yet.
Do not judge another person by a chapter God is still redeeming.
And do not answer a matter before hearing it.
The next time your finger moves toward the comment section before you've finished reading, pause for one moment and ask yourself:
That question alone may reveal more about your heart than the article ever could.
One day we will discover how many battles could have been avoided if someone had simply listened a little longer.
